newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy employers see little way of avoiding strike.
newsitem.headline: Italy employers see little way of avoiding strike.

text.p: The eight hour strike called by metalworkers and engineering unions for September 27 looks certain to go ahead, the chairman of the Italian employers federation, Confindustria, said on Thursday.
"Time is pressing and I don't see any way out," Giorgio Fossa told reporters at a news conference. "I'm more pessimistic about this than I was a week ago," he added.
Negotiations between trades unions and employers over the renewal of contracts for some 1.5 million engineer and metalworkers broke down earlier on Thursday.
Unions have demanded an overall wage rise of 10.1 percent for their members over the next two years, while employers have offered between seven and nine percent.
"The two sides are too far apart to find a solution in the short-term. I hope that in October we'll be able to find a solution," Fossa said after an executive meeting at Confindustria.
He added that given current economic conditions, companies could not afford the union demands.

"It's not that we don't want to renew contracts, it's just that with (that type of) pay increase, factories risk closing in a few months time because they can't afford to stay in the market," Fossa said. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
